title: 1973 AHSME Problem 1
statement: A chord which is the perpendicular bisector of a radius of length \(12\) in a circle has length

solutions.text:
Let \(M\) be the midpoint of the chord and also the midpoint of the radius. The distance from the center \(O\) to \(M\) is \(6,\) while the circle’s radius is \(12.\) If \(A\) is one endpoint of the chord, then \[ AM=\sqrt{12^2-6^2}=6\sqrt3. \] The full chord has length \(2AM=12\sqrt3.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: The chord meets the radius halfway from the center and at a right angle
Find half the chord with the Pythagorean theorem, then double it
